title: Active Brownian Dynamics from a Hamiltonian Model: Transitioning from Equilibrium to Activity
authors: Antik Bhattacharya, Smarajit Karmakar, Jürgen Horbach
abstract: We introduce a Hamiltonian Active Brownian Particle (HABP) model that connects equilibrium dynamics with the non-equilibrium, two-dimensional overdamped behavior of standard Active Brownian Particles (ABPs). In equilibrium, the system follows overdamped Langevin equations that strictly satisfy the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. Coupling translational and rotational degrees of freedom to separate heat baths ($T_θ > T_{\textrm{tr}}$), drives the system out of equilibrium. In free space, matching the diffusion coefficients yields quantitative agreement with the ABP model in the limit $T_θ/T_{\textrm{tr}}\to \infty$, whereas in a harmonic potential, this matching is recovered even at finite temperature ratios. Entropy production analysis demonstrates that in the ABP limit, all energy injected by the swim force dissipates into the translational bath, leaving the rotational bath as a zero-cost entropy source. These insights provide the first steps toward equilibrium-inspired descriptions of active matter, facilitating the development of new theoretical frameworks to study activity-induced fluctuations, transport, and phase behavior in living and non-living soft matter systems far from equilibrium.
summary: This paper introduces the Hamiltonian Active Brownian Particle (HABP) model to provide a first-principles, equilibrium-inspired description of active matter. By coupling translational and rotational motion to separate heat baths, the model naturally transitions from equilibrium dynamics to non-equilibrium active states. The key achievement is quantifying activity through the entropy production rate and showing quantitative agreement with standard ABP models in the appropriate limits.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop an equilibrium-inspired theoretical framework to describe the non-equilibrium dynamics of active matter, specifically bridging the gap between standard Active Brownian Particles (ABPs) and an underlying Hamiltonian description.
main_result: The Hamiltonian Active Brownian Particle (HABP) model successfully reproduces the non-equilibrium behavior of ABPs when the translational and rotational baths are coupled with different temperatures, quantifying activity via entropy production.
method: The authors use overdamped Langevin equations derived from a Hamiltonian that couples translational and rotational degrees of freedom to separate heat baths, analyzing Mean Squared Displacements (MSDs) and entropy production rates.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by the Hamiltonian Active Brownian Particle (HABP) model, which includes position ($\vec{r}$), momentum ($\vec{p}$), and spin orientation ($\vec{S}$). The dynamics are governed by coupling to two baths at potentially different temperatures ($T_{tr}$ and $T_{	heta}$).
key_observables: Mean Squared Displacements (MSDs) for both translational and rotational motion, and the steady-state entropy production rate ($\dot{\sigma}$).
important_parameters: The temperature ratio ($T_{	heta}/T_{tr}$), the coupling constant ($K$), the trap strength ($\lambda$), and the damping coefficients ($\gamma_{tr}, \gamma_{	heta}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on deriving Langevin equations from a Hamiltonian and making approximations in the non-equilibrium limit, such as assuming rotational dynamics are noise-dominated for calculating $\langle\vec{S} \cdot \vec{r}angle$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the MSDs for HABP vs. ABP across varying rotational temperatures, showing crossovers from diffusive to ballistic regimes. Other figures plot Van Hove correlation functions and analyze MSDs in a harmonic potential.
paper_structure:
The paper first establishes the HABP model and its equilibrium properties, showing agreement with fluctuation-dissipation theorems. It then analyzes the non-equilibrium limit by setting $T_{	heta} 
eq T_{tr}$, demonstrating the emergence of activity and calculating the resulting entropy production. Finally, it extends the framework to interacting particles in a harmonic trap to study collective effects.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, Hamiltonian-based foundation for active matter, moving beyond purely phenomenological models by deriving activity from explicit thermodynamic asymmetries between coupled baths.
